events.title: Martin Luther is born in Eisleben
events.description: The man who would become the central figure of the Protestant Reformation was born in Eisleben, in what is now Germany. He was the son of a middle-class family and was raised in a devout household.
events.significance: Luther's challenge to the authority of the Catholic Church split Western Christianity and reshaped the religious, political and cultural life of Europe.

events.title: The Continental Congress creates the Marines
events.description: During the American Revolution, the Continental Congress passed a resolution to raise two battalions of Marines. Samuel Nicholas became the first Marine commandant. Recruiting is traditionally associated with Philadelphia's Tun Tavern.
events.significance: This date is celebrated each year as the birthday of the U.S. Marine Corps, one of the nation's most recognizable military forces.

events.title: Henry Wirz is hanged for war crimes
events.description: Major Henry Wirz, the commandant of the Andersonville prison camp in Georgia, was executed after a military trial. Thousands of Union prisoners had died at the camp from disease, exposure and starvation.
events.significance: Wirz was one of only three Civil War soldiers executed for war crimes. His case remains a landmark in discussions of the accountability of military commanders for the treatment of prisoners.

events.title: Stanley finds Livingstone
events.description: In Ujiji, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, journalist Henry Morton Stanley found the Scottish missionary and explorer David Livingstone. Livingstone had been out of contact with the outside world for years. Stanley is said to have greeted him with the famous words "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"
events.significance: The meeting became one of the most famous episodes in the European exploration of Africa and a defining moment in the history of newspaper-sponsored adventure.

events.title: Sesame Street premieres on American television
events.description: The educational children's program made its debut on PBS. It was created by Joan Ganz Cooney and Lloyd Morrisett and featured Jim Henson's Muppets alongside live actors.
events.significance: Sesame Street showed that television could be a powerful tool for early education. It grew into a global institution that has reached children in many countries.
